notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 05/08/2026
Patient: Regine Strosin, 65-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 05/08/2026. The study was conducted to assess sleep quality and identify any sleep-disordered breathing events.

Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 47.3 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 11% of all events. These findings indicate severe sleep apnea with a notable proportion of central and mixed apneas.

Sleep architecture showed normal distribution of sleep stages without significant fragmentation. No other abnormalities were observed during the study.

In conclusion, the patient exhibits severe sleep apnea requiring further clinical evaluation and management.

notes.title: Sleep Medicine Consultation
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/12/2026
Patient: Regine Strosin, 65-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of ongoing sleep-disordered breathing despite CPAP therapy.

History:
Ms. Strosin has been using CPAP therapy for obstructive sleep apnea. She reports consistent nightly use of the device.

Findings:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 26.3 events/hour on CPAP at 12 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Assessment:
The patient continues to experience significant residual apnea-hypopnea events despite adherence to CPAP therapy at an adequate pressure setting.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options including bilevel positive airway pressure or advanced modalities.
2. Reassess mask fit and adherence to therapy.
3. Schedule follow-up sleep study to evaluate effectiveness of any changes.
4. Provide patient education on sleep hygiene and device maintenance.

Summary:
Ms. Strosin demonstrates persistent obstructive sleep apnea with significant residual events on CPAP therapy, necessitating further evaluation and management adjustments.
